subject: PulseLine: deployment mode & audit intake — next steps and evidence list
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@pulselinehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: PulseLine: deployment mode & audit intake — next steps and evidence list

Thanks for the call today — appreciate you walking through PulseLine's primary constraint: PHI at rest plus an internal audit window that requires forensic logs for 12 months. From our side that mostly drives the hosting conversation (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Quick recap of the options we discussed and what we need to assess next: 
- Hosted API: fastest path but requires us to validate whether the Hosted environment and BAA controls meet your SOC2/log retention needs; we can provide SOC2 artifacts and a BAA but there are tradeoffs on data residency and customer-managed keys.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): reduces shared-tenant concerns and gives predictable throughput; supports customer key management (KMS) integrations but still runs in Redwood-managed infra.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full isolation, aligns best with rigorous audit needs but is longer lead time and requires infra footprint on your side or a Private deployment agreement.

Action items I promised on the call: 
1) Initial evidence pack from Redwood (SOC2 summary, BAA template, sample audit logs format) — attached.
2) Clarify the exact length and granularity of logs you need (audit fields, retention policy, exporter format).
3) Jordan to scope Dedicated throughput and KMS options (est. timeline + infra footprint).
4) Neha to confirm any additional audit artifacts beyond SOC2 + audit logs (vulnerability scans, pen test reports).

Request: Ryan / Asha — can you confirm the internal audit's acceptance criteria for a partner-hosted service vs a private deployment? For example: is a signed BAA + SOC2 Type II + 12-month immutable logs sufficient, or do you require customer-controlled HSMs and on-prem hosting? That will determine recommended path and timeline.

Next steps: I'll loop in Jordan and Neha with specifics once you confirm acceptance criteria. If it helps, we can also produce a short decision matrix (risk vs time-to-production vs cost) for your security and procurement teams.

Cheers,

Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: SOC2-Type2-summary-2025.pdf (pdf) — BAA-template-Redwood.docx (docx) — network-diagram-pulseline.png (png)
From: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@pulselinehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.p@pulselinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PulseLine: deployment mode & audit intake — next steps and evidence list

Thanks Soojin — good summary. Asha and I discussed briefly. A couple points from the audit team: 
- Acceptance criteria: signed BAA + SOC2 Type II is the baseline. For production with PHI we *prefer* customer-managed encryption keys (KMS) and at-rest encryption we can validate.
- Logs: 12 months immutable retention, with the following minimum fields: timestamp (UTC), request ID, user id (internal reference), model id & version, token counts (input/output), action type (generate/embed/stream), and a SHA256 hash of the prompt (to avoid storing raw PHI where possible). Exportable as newline-delimited JSON is preferred.
- For Dedicated vs Hosted: audit will accept Dedicated with KMS + the log export if you can guarantee retention and immutability; Hosted requires us to show that keys and logs are segregated and that you can support legal hold requests.

Can Jordan send a short doc with what Dedicated provides today (KMS integrations, retention policy, SLA) and an estimated timeline for Private VPC onboarding if we go that route? Also Neha — if you can confirm what additional artifacts you can provide (pen test summary, vuln fix cadence), that will help speed procurement.

Ryan
CTO, PulseLine Health
ryan.cole@pulselinehealth.com

Thanks — that's very helpful and clear. Jordan, can you put together a short one-pager (1–2 pages) that covers: 
- Current Dedicated capabilities: KMS integrations (AWS KMS / GCP KMS), how keys are scoped per-tenant, encryption-at-rest guarantees.
- Log export details: format (newline-delimited JSON), retention controls, immutability options (WORM + archiving) and S3 lifecycle/backups.
- Private VPC/on-prem onboarding steps and realistic lead times (approx. effort, roles involved, and hardware footprint if on-prem).

Neha — can you attach the latest pen test summary and confirm cadence for vuln scanning and patch windows (monthly/quarterly)? If there are any artifacts you can't share publicly, note that and we'll set up an NDA + secure share.

Ryan / Asha — if you can confirm whether PulseLine would be open to starting on Dedicated (to get into production faster) and later moving to Private VPC if required after a procurement sign-off, that will help us build a phased plan.

I'll draft the decision matrix as promised and share by Monday.

Best,
Soojin

Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — capability snapshot (short)

Ryan — attaching a short capability snapshot here (inline summary + attachments on request). High-level: 
- Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated): 
  * KMS: supports AWS KMS and GCP KMS. Keys are tenant-scoped and can be rotated on demand. We can integrate with customer KMS via IAM federation for key access controls.
  * Logs: real-time export to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets or to Redwood-managed archival with signed attestations. Exports are newline-delimited JSON by default; we can include the fields you requested. Retention is configurable (default 90 days) — we offer extended retention add-ons to meet 12-month retention with immutability options (WORM) and cross-region backups.
  * Timeline: Dedicated can be provisioned in ~2–3 weeks for a reserved pool (if capacity available); KMS integration and log routing typically add 1–2 weeks of engineering that we include in the onboarding plan.

- Private VPC / On-prem: 
  * Offers full network isolation, VPC peering options, and support for on-prem deployments. Requires a short professional services engagement (2–6 weeks depending on ops readiness) plus infra procurement if on-prem.
  * Provides the strongest audit posture (customer controls keys, local log retention). Lead time is longer but is the recommended path for customers who must demonstrate hardware-level control to auditors.

Attachments we can provide immediately: SOC2-Type2-summary-2025.pdf, BAA-template-Redwood.docx, sample-log-schema-ndjson.txt. Neha — tagging you to attach pen test and vuln cadence.

If you're comfortable, we can draft a phased plan: start on Dedicated with KMS and 12-month WORM retention while we kick off the Private VPC procurement track in parallel. That reduces time-to-production while preserving a path to full isolation.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
